rows.question: When I paste a link to import a recipe from a website, in what order does the app try its different ways of pulling the recipe out of the page, and what happens if one of them throws an error?
If I add the same thing to my grocery list twice, what decides whether the two entries get combined into a single line instead of staying separate?
How does the server work out how long to wait before kicking off its once-a-day housekeeping jobs?
When restoring a backup, what happens to rows whose references point at records that aren't present in the backup data?
When moving my recipes over from Paprika, how do the photos stored inside the export file end up attached to the newly created recipes?
What happens to an account after someone enters the wrong password too many times in a row — does it get frozen, and when does the counter reset?
What are the lower and upper limits on how long a person stays signed in before they have to log in again?
When login is delegated to a corporate directory server, what stops someone from signing in as a known user by simply leaving the password blank?
After a user changes their password, how does the API turn away requests that still carry a login token issued before the change?
Is it possible to trade a long-lived API key for a normal, renewable browser login session, and where is that prevented?
Where does the admin backup API make sure a requested backup file name can't point to a file outside the backups directory?
When someone asks for a random recipe to fill a meal plan slot, how are the household's planning rules turned into the recipe search that picks it?
What checks apply when a household manager tries to change another member's permissions, for example a member of a different household, or their own account?
Can a meal plan entry be saved without linking a recipe, and what has to be filled in instead?
What happens if a recipe is given a name made up only of emoji or punctuation, so no URL-friendly identifier can be built from it?
If a webhook's daily send time is submitted as a full timestamp with a time zone rather than a plain time of day, how is it interpreted?
Where is an ingredient amount like 2.75 turned into a mixed fraction such as 2 3/4 for display, and when is a decimal shown instead?
How does saving a new recipe deal with a name that clashes with an existing recipe in the same group?
When list results are sorted randomly, how does the app keep that shuffled order consistent while the client pages through them?
Which meal planning rules count as applying to, say, a Tuesday dinner, including rules that don't name a specific day or meal type?
When a user sorts or filters recipes by rating, whose rating is used — their own, or the recipe's overall rating?
When a user is marked as an administrator, what happens to their other permission flags like inviting, managing and organizing?
How is a recipe's overall rating value computed from the ratings individual users have given it, and are zero ratings counted?
What happens to an ingredient substitute that refers to a food which was deleted or belongs to a different group?
Where is the search-friendly copy of a saved recipe, food or unit name produced, with accents stripped, punctuation turned into spaces, everything lowercased and the length capped?
Which kinds of network addresses are refused by default when the server fetches a user-supplied URL, such as a recipe link or a webhook target?
What does the downloader do, step by step, when a recipe site keeps blocking it with bot-protection challenges?
Where are the smaller preview versions of a recipe photo generated when an image is saved, and what sizes are they?
Where is it decided which recurring background jobs run once a day, once an hour, and every few minutes?
What text-direction and plural-food display settings does the server fall back to when a request's language header isn't a locale it recognizes?
In a saved filter, how can I express a date relative to today, like thirty days ago, instead of a fixed date, and how does that get turned into a real timestamp?
How does the app tack details like the event type, the event's ID and a timestamp onto an outgoing Apprise notification address?
Is there a cap on how many ticked-off entries a shopping list keeps around, and which ones get thrown away once there are too many?
When someone pastes a link to one of our recipes into a chat app or social network, where does the server put together the preview card's title, description and picture?
What stops a request for a file attached to a recipe from reaching files outside that recipe's folder, or from being opened in the browser as a live web page?
Who is allowed to generate an invite code for joining a household, and in which situations is that request refused?
If the AI model returns its JSON answer wrapped in a markdown code block or with stray null characters, where is that cleaned up before the answer is parsed?
Postgres sometimes gives back timestamps ending in an offset like +02 with no minutes. Where does the code patch those up so the API models don't reject them?
On SQLite, what format are record IDs actually written to the database in, and how does that differ from Postgres?
After a database upgrade, what happens to meal plans, recipes or comments that still point at a user account that no longer exists?
When a unit like tablespoon or quart is added without any conversion details, how does the app work out how it compares to other measurements?
If someone edits a saved AI provider and doesn't send its secret key again, does the stored key get wiped?
If I supply a full Postgres connection string as an override and the password contains characters like @ or /, how is the password handled so the URL still works?
How do translated messages choose between singular and plural wording depending on a number?
For the command-line tool that regenerates recipe pictures, how does it decide which recipes actually need their images redone?
